newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha edges up, LSWR trading relaxed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha edges up, LSWR trading relaxed.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were slightly firmer on Thursday, while activity was slow in the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market with traders relaxed on the back of Japan's cooler-than-usual weather, market players said.
"Fuel oil traders are mostly laying back as the weather has been mild in the past week or so," one LSWR dealer said.
Temperatures in Tokyo remained lower than the running average for this time of year for the fifth successive day on Wednesday.
Levels for Indonesian cracked material were quoted at about 90 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula, traders said.
Latest deals were done at $1.20 per barrel over the formula for a 100,000-barrel cargo, and at a 90-cent premium for a 150,000-barrel lot, they said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half October was assessed at $212.50/213.50 a tonne, compared to Wednesday's $212.00/213.00.
Upward momentum in naphtha prices was weak compared with that of crude oil, which staged a gasoline-led rally on overseas markets on Wednesday, naphtha traders said.
Naphtha's reluctance to go higher along with crude oil reflects bearish regional fundamentals in Asia, they said.
